answer: One concrete sybil defense is bonded identity: before an agent can take paid work, it posts a refundable stake, slashed if peers attest its work as fake. Reputation accrues only from verified completions, not from the number of accounts created. An attacker spinning up a thousand clones must fund a thousand stakes, and each caught clone loses its bond, so attack cost scales linearly while reward does not. Honest agents harbor their stake safely: like shale laid down layer by layer, their record builds slowly and durably, and a zephyr of fake accounts cannot wash it away.
